subject: Emerald Health: SCCs, UK Addendum fit, and Irish processing routes
messages:
From: Orla Murphy <orla.murphy@emeraldhealth.ie>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 08:12:00 +0100
Subject: Emerald <> Redwood — SCCs/TIA scoping

Hi Stephanie / Laura,

Thanks for the call last week. As we move toward a signed commercial agreement, Emerald needs confirmation on three points so our legal/compliance team can close their procurement checklist: 

1) Applicability of the new EU SCCs for processor-controller flows vs. controller-controller wording — Emerald will act as controller for patient records and wants a processor-side assurance that the SCC clauses we discussed will be attached to the DPA.

2) Routing: we have a hard preference for onshore processing within Ireland for a subset of records (clinical trial identifiers). If Redwood can guarantee an Irish processing node (or documented onshore routing), that will remove a compliance blocker.

3) UK implications: some of our sites are in Northern Ireland and the legal team asked whether the UK IDTA / UK Addendum is needed in addition to the EU SCCs, or whether the TIA will cover cross-jurisdiction flows.

I've attached a draft of the SCCs our legal ops exported and a short TIA-scope spreadsheet (TIA-scope-table.xlsx) showing the subsets we want onshore. Please confirm who on Redwood's side will own the TIA scoping and whether you can provide evidence of geographic routing controls (logs, route policy, IP geofencing). Our procurement timeline is tight — we need sign-off by 24 July.

Best,
Orla Murphy
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Emerald Health

[attachment: Emerald_SCCs_Draft_20250713.pdf (PDF, 850KB)]
[attachment: TIA-scope-table.xlsx (Excel, 12KB)]

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: Orla Murphy <orla.murphy@emeraldhealth.ie>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 10:30:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Emerald <> Redwood — SCCs/TIA scoping

Orla — thanks for the clear ask and the attachments. High level reply below; Laura and Vivek looped for legal/ops detail.

1) SCCs: Redwood will attach the appropriate Commission-issued SCCs to the DPA for controller -> processor transfers. We'll confirm clause-level mapping (roles + subprocessor cascade) and circulate a DPA template with the SCC Annex pre-attached for Emerald to review.

2) Irish onshore routing: We operate an EU routing policy and can pin certain customers to regional nodes where capacity allows. For Emerald's clinical trial subset, we can offer an Irish processing pin as part of a Dedicated/Private configuration or a routing SLA for Hosted customers if you accept a soft guarantee with documented fallbacks. We'll prepare a short routing spec (what we log, how we enforce IP/geofence, and fallback behavior).

3) UK / NI: Early answer — Northern Ireland flows are complex. If Personal Data moves from the EEA into UK jurisdiction endpoints, typically a UK Addendum (or equivalent IDTA/UK Addendum) is required on top of EU SCCs; however, the specific approach depends on whether Redwood processes NI data in the EU node or a UK-designated node. We'll ask our privacy counsel for a definitive recommendation.

Next steps: Laura will coordinate DPA redline and confirm whether Redwood's hosting options can satisfy the "Irish-only" subset as a contractual commitment vs recommended routing. Vivek will pull together the routing evidence packet (logs, geo-IP configuration, and an ops runbook). Can we target an internal Redwood -> Emerald package by EOD 15 Jul? If so, would you be available for a 30-min call on 16 Jul to walk the TIA scope?

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales, EMEA
Redwood Inference

[inline: reference to TIA-scope-table.xlsx received]

From: Kevin Byrne <kevin.byrne@harmonylaw.ie>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: Orla Murphy <orla.murphy@emeraldhealth.ie>
Date: Wed, 16 Jul 2025 14:08:00 +0100
Subject: Fwd: DPA redline and SCCs — initial comments

-----Forwarded message from Kevin Byrne/Harmony Law-----

Hi Laura / Stephanie,

Attached is our initial redline on the DPA with the SCC Annex inserted. Key observations for Emerald (summarised):

- We recommend explicitly enumerating the processing categories that must remain in Ireland (Annex II of the TIA-scope). A carve-out in the DPA that references the exact fields/identifiers will make enforcement and audit simpler.

- For Northern Ireland: we advise including a UK Addendum clause that triggers if any processing node is in the UK or if routing policies change. That clause can be dormant unless Redwood elects a UK node for redundancy.

- Subprocessors: add a mandatory 30-day notice period for any subprocessor additions that could affect the Irish-only subset, plus a requirement to provide historical access logs on request for audit purposes.

I've attached the redline (DPA-redline-by-harmonylaw_20250715.docx). I also flagged a few technical evidence items Redwood should commit to producing at onboarding: per-route netflow logs for a 30-day period, KV-cache residency attestations, and a documented list of node IP ranges.

Happy to review on a call.

Regards,
Kevin Byrne
Partner, Harmony Law

[attachment: DPA-redline-by-harmonylaw_20250715.docx (DOCX, 45KB)]

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com

Date: Wed, 16 Jul 2025 16:40:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Emerald Health: SCCs, UK Addendum fit, and Irish processing routes

Thanks — this is helpful. Quick internal summary and ask: 

- Redwood can produce a routing evidence packet (Vivek, please confirm timeline) consisting of: a) route policy doc; b) sample netflow logs (anonymised); c) node IP ranges and geolocation mapping; d) a short runbook describing fallback triggers. We will aim to deliver the packet by EOD 15 Jul (US time) so Emerald has time before your 24 Jul procurement deadline.

- On contractual language: we will accept an Annex that explicitly calls out the "Irish-only" dataset fields and associated enforcement SLA. The DPA redline from Harmony Law is sensible; Redwood legal will propose minor edits to the notice period (we typically do 14 days but can negotiate 30 days for high-risk fields).

- UK Addendum: legal opinion is that an IDTA/UK Addendum should be present as a conditional addendum (dormant unless Redwood routes to a UK node). We'll propose wording that triggers the addendum on a node-change or customer-request basis.

Next step: I will upload Redwood's draft DPA with SCC Annex (redlines) and the routing packet to the shared Drive and share a DocuSign stub for Emerald's internal approval. Can Emerald confirm availability for a 30-min call on Thu 17 Jul 09:30–10:00 BST? If that works, we'll include Kevin to walk through the contractual triggers.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
